headline: High: Flowise’s writable, networked orchestration can leak or misroute data, while godot_rl_agents adds no compensating controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write files and run browser/tool nodes, and its flows may ingest uploaded files or HTTP content as inputs. godot_rl_agents has no documented ingestion surface, so direct hijack is not evidenced; however, if Flowise outputs are bridged into a game-agent pipeline or shared workspace, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are copied into a shared workspace consumed by godot_rl_agents
IF Flowise browser/tool outputs are parsed as instructions by downstream automation
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Flowise-generated text into downstream prompts
Use a read-only handoff file format with explicit delimiters
Add a human review step before any downstream execution
Separate the two agents into distinct workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all Flowise outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and it has broad network egress to model providers and HTTP tools. godot_rl_agents documents no data classes or egress, so the pairwise leak path is one-sided but plausible if sensitive Flowise inputs are routed into the game agent’s environment or logs. Because the interaction is undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Flowise chatflow inputs include secrets or uploaded files
IF godot_rl_agents receives those artifacts via shared storage or logs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of Flowise chatflows
Store shared artifacts in a separate redacted directory
Turn off verbose logging for both agents
Restrict Flowise HTTP tools to allowlisted endpoints
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the server filesystem and uses server datastore shared across instances; godot_rl_agents exposes no write or network capabilities in the profile. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so a direct write-write conflict is not established. The only plausible conflict is unusual deployment sharing, which keeps severity low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory
IF a shared datastore is mounted into both runtimes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Mount shared storage read-only for one agent
Avoid concurrent writes to the same git or database state
Check deployment manifests for overlapping volumes
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer that can emit tool outputs and chatflow results, while godot_rl_agents is a game/simulation agent with no documented verification gate. If Flowise output is fed into the game agent as authoritative input, downstream actions or training decisions could propagate errors. Because no direct evidence shows this exact handoff, the risk is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents consumes Flowise outputs without validation
IF Flowise-generated facts are used to drive downstream actions or training
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on all Flowise outputs
Log and compare outputs against a baseline before acting
Limit downstream actions to non-destructive modes
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and rejection thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys, tool credentials, and chatflow inputs/outputs, which can create residency or retention obligations. godot_rl_agents documents no sensitive data classes or compliance claims, so the compliance issue is primarily on Flowise’s side. Without evidence of regulated data flowing through the pair, this is a low-severity mismatch rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Flowise chatflows
IF retention or residency policies differ between the Flowise deployment and the game-agent environment
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Flowise flows
Set short retention on Flowise logs and artifacts
Document where each agent stores outputs
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
